conventions.convention: SI units; x⁰=ct, c>0, μ₀>0 and ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹. μ₀ is experimentally determined, not assigned an exact numerical value.

Separated physical fields are componentwise real parts of amplitudes times exp(i(βx₃−ωt)), with ω>0 and possibly complex β. Positive real β propagates along +e_z; Im β controls spatial exponential decay.

Rectangular PEC conditions apply on open faces: n×E=0 and n·B=0 with outward normals. Corners are not declared C¹ boundary points. The energy reflection class includes the specified electric/magnetic parities and distributionally zero divergences; interior smoothness alone supplies no continuous reflected trace.

TE, TM and TEM are relative to the named longitudinal axis. TE rectangle indices satisfy m,n≥0 and (m,n)≠(0,0); TM indices satisfy m,n≥1. The constant Neumann scalar belongs to the scalar basis but is not a nonzero positive-frequency TE mode.

The longitudinal Fourier transform has negative sign and 2π normalization, β=2πξ. Transverse characters use unnormalized torus-area integration; the physical reflection-field norm is one quarter of the extended norm.

Countable Choice is retained for the interval/rectangle, Fourier, surface-measure and point-source interfaces. Full Choice is retained for the smooth-cavity spectral realization. Its zero eigenspaces and the static magnetic kernel are retained.

A retarded point datum has an all-time C³ trajectory z:ℝ→ℝ³ and one uniform bound |z′|≤v_*<c. Fields and retarded geometric formulas are evaluated off Γ; κ=1−n·β is uniformly positive. Pointwise subluminality alone is insufficient.

Compact-source far-zone limits hold at fixed retarded time u. Replacing the shifted current moment V(n,u) by p″(u) incurs the explicit absolute D(u) error; slow motion alone does not establish its smallness.

General-event emitted power is the κ₀-weighted far-zone flux per emission time, not an asserted mechanical energy-loss rate. At an instantaneous-rest event κ₀=1. The orbit thought experiment adopts its mechanical loss balance separately.
The tensor dictionary uses η=diag(−1,1,1,1), F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c, Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ and j=(cρ,J). Consequently ∂μFμν=−μ₀jν. Only proper orthochronous inertial changes are adopted.

Observer covectors are e_a=F_ab n^b and b_a=(*F)_ab n^b; measured rest vectors are E_n=c e♯ and B_n=−b♯ under the explicitly adopted ideal-detector assumption. Orthogonality to n does not mean zero laboratory temporal components.

The spatial stress-energy block is Tⁱʲ=−σᵢⱼ. Zero total divergence gives a slice balance retaining signed side flux; slice totals are constant exactly when the net side flux vanishes on every subinterval.

load_bearing.statement: The definition fixes rectangular guide and cavity regions, outward open-wall normals, the declared PEC conditions n×E=0 and n·B=0, the divergence-free zero-normal-B reflection class, axis-relative TE/TM/TEM and the separated real-part phasor convention. It asserts no field equation or mode existence/completeness.

The framework adopts the retarded branch with no independently prescribed homogeneous addition, including the explicitly declared weak point-source branch. This is an additional physical selection, not a deduction or an existence/uniqueness theorem.

Under Countable Choice, for a prescribed all-time C³ uniformly subluminal point worldline and the retarded selection, φ=C/(κr), A=βφ/c and E=C[(1−|β|²)(n−β)/(κ³r²)+n×((n−β)×β̇)/(cκ³r)], B=n×E/c off Γ. The fields are C¹ there, their velocity remainder is uniformly O(r⁻²) in direction at a fixed emission event, and their locally integrable extensions satisfy the declared distributional point-source Maxwell equations.

For the fixed tensor dictionary, jointly C¹ fields and continuous sources, the four smooth laboratory Maxwell equations hold iff ∂μFμν=−μ₀jν and ∂λFμν+∂μFνλ+∂νFλμ=0. Both systems are form-invariant under the stated constant proper orthochronous inertial component law; weak and singular branches are excluded.

Under Countable Choice, jointly smooth conserved sources supported in B̄_a×[t₀,T] have smooth retarded potentials satisfying their sourced wave equations and Lorenz gauge, hence smooth Maxwell fields. They vanish before t₀, equal the zero-data Cauchy solution at each earlier time, and have total charge zero.

In the declared lossless isotropic material-rest model, the displayed TE and TM rectangular profiles with their stated index restrictions and β²=εμω²−k_mn² give smooth source-free macroscopic Maxwell fields satisfying the open-wall PEC conditions. Real β exists exactly at or above ω_c=k_c/√(εμ), is nonzero above cutoff, and below cutoff the roots are imaginary. No completeness is asserted.

Assuming Countable Choice, the cosine family indexed by m≥0 and sine family indexed by m≥1 are orthogonal complete systems in real L²(0,L), L>0; all four sine/cosine product families with their respective index ranges are orthogonal complete systems in L² of a positive-sided rectangle.

Assuming Countable Choice, polar measure on S² satisfies ∫f(n₃)dσ=2π∫₋₁¹f(u)du for continuous f, the stated linear and quadratic weighted moments, σ(S²)=4π, ∫nᵢnⱼdσ=(4π/3)δᵢⱼ and ∫|n×a|²dσ=(8π/3)|a|² for real a.

For the declared constant scalar Ohmic material model, the rectangular reflection class and the full-Choice smooth PEC modal realization have unique continuous energy-space evolutions and compact-time modal convergence. U(t₁)+σ∫ₜ₀ᵗ¹‖E‖²dt=U(t₀). Positive modes decay for σ>0; electric zero modes decay exponentially and magnetic kernel data remain static. Arbitrary associated second-order data are distinguished from first-order compatibility.

For the declared compact smooth conserved retarded source, p′=∫J, p″=∫J_t and |V(n,u)−p″(u)|≤D(u). The dipole electric-field error is at most Γ_E/r²+μ₀D/(4πr), and the fixed-retarded-time power is μ₀|p″|²/(6πc)+R with |R|≤μ₀(2|p″|D+D²)/(4πc).

For the specified passive boost and field dictionary, E′∥=E∥, B′∥=B∥, E′⊥=γ(E+v×B)⊥ and B′⊥=γ(B−v×E/c²)⊥. The item proves the arbitrary-direction boost, proper-rotation factorization, invariance of |B|²−|E|²/c² and E·B, and form invariance of smooth Maxwell equations on the chart overlap.

For constant q, supplied m>0 and a C² future timelike worldline obeying the adopted coupling in a prescribed external C¹ field, p=mγv satisfies dp/dt=q(E+v×B) and d(γmc²)/dt=qE·v. The four-velocity norm is preserved. The stated uniform low-speed momentum and energy bounds are pointwise expansions, not trajectory-stability results.

concerns.concern: The task declares prerequisites em-electrostatic-boundaries-and-conductors and em-vacuum-waves-and-polarization, but the page and its owned items provide no identifiable citation or exact proposition use from either page. The PEC definition instead explicitly uses pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps and declares its idealization. These two seams therefore lack a citing clause whose fidelity can be checked; identify the intended supplier use or reconcile the prerequisite records.

The orbit paragraph says the cubic 'reaches r=0 at the finite reduced-model time' and calls collapse 'a mathematical property of (H)'. The cited thought experiment explicitly restricts r to its positive-radius validity interval and assigns the zero-radius limit to the maximal scalar-ODE continuation after dropping the validity-window inequalities. The paragraph's subsequent caveat helps, but it should preserve that formal-continuation distinction explicitly.

seams_checked.note: No identifiable proposition citation from this declared prerequisite occurs in the owned guide page/items. PEC is declared locally with a qualified material-jump interpretation; this is a missing seam anchor, not an identified false conductor claim.

Candidates restate D=εE, B=μH, the lossless material-rest branch and the four source-free macroscopic equations. Ohmic consumers separately adopt their weak realization; the PEC definition preserves stationary-jump normal signs and excludes treating corners or the infinite-conductivity limit as supplied.

The declared page prerequisite has no identifiable cited proposition in the guide carriers. No vacuum plane-wave result is restated or improperly strengthened; an exact intended use remains unrecorded.
pthm-em-dipole-radiation F1–F2 preserve thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux's smooth compact spacetime support, continuity hypothesis, shifted current V, r≥2a bounds and fixed-retarded-time flux limit.

The dynamic dipole integral is defined locally and explicitly called the fixed-time analogue of def-em-electric-moments. No dynamical identity is attributed to the static definition; p′=∫J is proved from continuity.

S=E×B/μ₀ is preserved. The point-field theorem explicitly licenses smooth local Poynting balance only on product neighborhoods disjoint from Γ, with zero local sources; no singular self-work or global finite-energy balance is inferred.

The selection postulate and compact-source theorem preserve E=−∇φ−A_t, B=curl A, G=div A+c⁻²φ_t and W=c⁻²∂t²−Δ. Lorenz decoupling is used with G=0, which the compact-source proof establishes from continuity.

The Liénard–Wiechert consumer preserves the all-time C³ uniform speed bound, off-worldline domain, exact history-pairing interpretation, signed C, κ denominator and directional uniform remainder at fixed emission event. Weak Maxwell admissibility is sourced separately.

Observer F5–F8 preserve the future-null phase covector, ideal reading postulates, inertial-observer scope, arbitrary-direction Doppler/aberration formulas, zero-motion case and both transverse protocols.
